messages:
alex: quick FYI — i'm planning to migrate inference-worker from Deployment -> StatefulSet so we keep per-pod PVCs. want a quick sanity check on rollout settings and PDB interactions before i open the PR. thinking ordinal start, podManagementPolicy: Parallel, and rollingUpdate.partition for canary.

maria: +1 on keeping PVCs. what are you thinking for replicas and partition size? also we need to consider HPA if any autoscaling is on.

alex: currently prod has replicas: 6. plan: start with replicas: 6, canary partition 1 (so partition: 5) for a 1-pod canary. HPA is off for this service (we scale manually) so simpler.

sam: question — with podManagementPolicy: Parallel we won't get ordered start guarantees. do we need ordinals for init data migrations?

alex: good call. we have an init job that seeds local cache on first boot but it can run concurrently. we only need stable identity for PVC naming, not strict ordering. parallel is fine and speeds up capacity rebuilds.

olivia: what about readiness/startup probes? previous rollout caused slow pods to be marked ready too early and traffic dropped.

alex: will tighten startupProbe and add a startup delay. e.g.:
```yaml
startupProbe:
  httpGet:
    path: /health/startup
    port: 8080
  failureThreshold: 30
  periodSeconds: 10
readinessProbe:
  httpGet:
    path: /health/ready
    port: 8080
  initialDelaySeconds: 10
  periodSeconds: 5
```
this gives ~5min for startup checks before kube marks ready.

maria: nice. also set resources so kube schedules predictably. previous autoscaler hit OOMs.

alex: setting requests: cpu 500m, memory 2Gi; limits: cpu 2, memory 6Gi for now. will monitor.

sam: PDB? we have a global PDB allowing maxUnavailable: 1 for this app — with replicas 6 and partitioning we should be ok. but confirm PDB targets the statefulset label selector.

alex: yep will add a PDB that references the same app label. PDB yaml in the PR.

olivia: secrets wiring — PVCs will stay, but the secret mount path changed last quarter. need to confirm the StatefulSet uses the same projected volume mount as before (so secret rotation keeps working).

alex: thanks — i'll include the projected secret volume block. snippet i'll use in helm values:
```yaml
statefulset:
  podManagementPolicy: Parallel
  rollingUpdate:
    partition: 5
  volumeClaimTemplates:
    - name: data
      spec: ...
  projectedSecrets:
    - name: inference-creds
      mountPath: /etc/creds
```

maria: small nit — for rollingUpdate.partition: 5 that means only 1 pod updates (good). but if you later change replicas count you'll need to recalc partition. mention that in PR.

alex: noted, will mention and add a make-target to update partition based on replicas.

devops-bot: CI triggered: https://ci/redwood/12345 — helm template + k8s-lint passed.

sam: can we also add a preStop hook to gracefully drain in-flight requests? a 10s sleep + notify to proxy should help.

alex: yes, preStop: exec: ["/bin/sh","-c","sleep 10; /usr/bin/drain-proxy"] will be added.

olivia: last ask — add an annotation to opt into the cache warmup job so the canary waits for warm cache before traffic. something like: `redwood/cache-warmup: "true"`

alex: good idea. i'll add that as a pod annotation and the job will watch for it.

maria: sounds solid. once PR is up tag me and @sam. schedule a 30m canary window during low traffic and we'll watch logs/latency. :thumbsup:

alex: will open PR in ~30m and request reviews. thanks all. :raised_hands:
